what.text: This page follows asylum seekers from Georgia in the United States: people who have asked for international protection and are waiting for a decision.
At the end of 2025, UNHCR counted 11031 Georgian asylum seekers in the United States, 38.2% of all asylum seekers from Georgia.
Refugees from Georgia, a separate group, live mostly in France, Germany, the United States and Ireland.

why.text: UCDP records armed conflict over South Ossetia territory in Georgia in 2004 and 2008, with the Republic of South Ossetia.
The fact pack records no armed conflict in Georgia in recent years, so it does not say why the number of asylum seekers grew.

when.text: UNHCR's series for this group starts in 2000 at 310 asylum seekers.
The figure reached its highest point, 16053, at the end of 2024, and the main years of displacement in the data are 2023 to 2025.

how.text: The sources don't say which routes people took or where they live in the United States.
Asylum seekers are counted separately from refugees, as year-end totals for the United States only.
